title.narrative: Kiribati Second Resilient Growth Development Policy Operation with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option

description.narrative: The development objectives and pillars of the Second Resilient Growth Development Policy Operation (DPO) with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option for Kiribati are to support the Government of Kiribati's (GOK) reforms to: (i) strengthen fiscal management, and (ii) promote inclusive and climate-resilient economic development. Strengthening fiscal management and promoting inclusive and climate resilient economic development are closely aligned with the GOK's key priorities. The prior actions in this DPO draw on lessons learned in previous Kiribati lending operations and from previous Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDOs) and include: (i) support should be coordinated amongst development partners; (ii) reforms should be spread across ministries to avoid overburdening any single one; (iii) technical assistance is needed to build capacity and improves the probability that reforms are successfully implemented; and (iv) reforms should be sequential, to help ensure they become embedded.

Results Indicator 1b. The lag in tabling the audited financial statements in Parliament after the end of the Financial Year.

comment.narrative: 2024 audited financial statements have not been tabled in Parliament as of 30 June 2026. In May 2026 the Audit office started auditing the 2024 financial statements. These were prepared using the old pre-IFMIS system, and so the efficiency gains from the IFMIS are not yet being realized. The 2024 audit must be complete before the 2025 audit is started. The first full year that the IFMIS was used was in 2025, so we anticipate the lag for tabling the FY2025 audited financial statements to be shorter, and shorter again for FY26.
